question: In the case of necessary goods, the law of demand cannot be operated. This was observed by the British economist:
solution:
The correct answer is **Sir Robert Giffen**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sir Robert Giffen:**

 
 
• Sir Robert Giffen is known for his observation related to the behavior of demand for necessary goods, which led to the concept of Giffen goods.
 
• Giffen goods are a type of inferior good for which an increase in the price results in an increase in quantity demanded, contrary to the law of demand.
 
• These goods are typically essential items, where the income effect outweighs the substitution effect, leading to higher demand even as prices rise.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Milton Friedman:**

 
 
• Milton Friedman was an American economist known for his work on consumption analysis, monetary history, and theory, and the complexity of stabilization policy. He did not focus on the law of demand in the context of necessary goods.
 
 
 
• **Irving Fisher:**
 
 
• Irving Fisher was an American economist who made important contributions to the theory of interest and capital. His work did not directly address the law of demand concerning necessary goods.
 
 
 
• **John Maynard Keynes:**
 
 
• John Maynard Keynes was a British economist whose ideas fundamentally changed the theory and practice of macroeconomics and economic policies. He is best known for his advocacy of government intervention to achieve full employment and stable prices, not for his work on the law of demand in relation to necessary goods.
